session_label: Aegis PMA · for Wed 4 Nov 2026 · AQE data to COB Tue 3 Nov

bottom_line.headline: Six names are advanced and none is buyable yet: SPY is down 3.18% over 20 days with dealers short gamma, so every entry waits for a completed hourly close above yesterday's high.
bottom_line.paragraph: Defensive groups lead (Healthcare, Staples, Real Estate, Utilities) while Technology and Communication Services are blocked at the sector gate, and two of the six advances, ROKU and DIS, sit in the blocked Communication Services group. SPY closed 754.35, 1.9% under the dealer gamma flip at 768.70, so moves in both directions get amplified. The one market-wide kill the committee carries (index under distribution) has no price, word or level an alert can watch, so it is a note, not a trigger.

what_happened.text: SPY closed 754.35, up 0.30% on Tuesday but down 3.18% over 20 days (63-day return -2.01%), while small caps (IWM) are down only 0.55% over 20 days.
The AQE equal-weight list fell 0.91% on Tuesday and only 58 of 350 names beat SPY, so the average stock did worse than the index on the day even though the five-day breadth ratio is improving.

Bond prices slipped 0.64% in five days (yields up), the dollar fund was flat (-0.38%), and gold (-3.5%), copper (-3.85%) and oil (-3.48%) all fell, while credit (HYG, -0.8%) sits under its 20-day average. The macro tape reads as a dollar squeeze (58% of its conditions met) contested by a growth scare within 12%, so there is no call.
VIX is 20.8 and VIX/VIX3M is 0.98 (0.92 five days ago, 0.85 a month ago): not calm, not yet stressed, and drifting up.

weather.text: Breadth is broadening (the average stock is keeping up with the index, 12 days into the regime, mid-range), trend funds are neutral and uncrowded, and the family is BROADENING_CARRY at a 1.00x multiplier on your own risk, but the fit is only partial because dealers are short gamma. The file is DEGRADED and its oldest leg is dated 2 Nov; positioning is dated 27 Oct.

SPY and QQQ are below their short-term averages on both charts, so the trend regime is a downtrend, and the one-word stance is withheld because the breadth inputs are stale (37% of the panel carries the 3 Nov bar; 95% is needed). Handbook doctrine, not an Aegis rule: if the market check is not green, do not push.

The light is red: SPY is 1.9% under the gamma flip (768.70) with the put wall at 750.00, 0.6% below the close, and QQQ is 5.4% under its flip (722.27) with its put wall at 680. The dealer side is a standard assumption, not observed data.

The average stock is beating the index only because the index is falling, dealers amplify both directions and trend funds are neutral, so any entry today is an entry against the index trend. It improves if SPY reclaims 768.70, the breadth ratio holds above its 20-day average, and Valen's breadth data returns so the stance can be read.

weather.stance: Read: Valen's one-word stance (RISK ON, NEUTRAL or RISK OFF) is withheld today because its breadth inputs are stale: only 1,600 of 4,314 panel tickers (37%) carry the 3 Nov bar and 95% is required. What is measured: SPY and QQQ are both below their short-term averages on the daily and weekly charts, so the trend regime is a downtrend (chop five days ago, uptrend a month ago). SPY sits 1.62 ATRs below its 50-day and QQQ 3.03 below, so neither is stretched, and VIX/VIX3M is 0.98, between calm (under 0.82) and stressed (over 1.00). Doctrine, quoted from the handbook and not an Aegis rule: if the market check is not green, do not push; for a momentum book that makes today's entries counter-trend.
weather.gex: Read: The light is red. SPY closed 754.35, 1.9% under the gamma flip at 768.70, and dealers are net short gamma (about -7.49 billion), so they sell into falls and buy into rises and moves get amplified both ways. The put wall at 750.00 is 0.6% below the close, and losing it removes the cushion; the call wall at 770.00 is 2.1% above, and a reclaim of 768.70 is what calms the tape. QQQ is 5.4% under its flip at 722.27 with its put wall at 680 and call wall at 700. The dealer side is a standard assumption, not observed data.
weather.heartbeat: Read: Breadth (the average stock against the index, RSP/SPY) is broadening, 12 days into the regime, up 2.85% over 5 days, 6.65% over 20 and 2.03% over 60, mid-range in its 12-month span with confidence 0.65. The ratio is 2.8% under its 12-month high and its 20-day average sits 3.4% below it, and a cross below that average is what would end the call. What it means for a momentum book: the average stock is outperforming because the cap-weighted index is falling (SPY -3.18% in 20 days, IWM -0.55%), so own the average stock rather than the leaders, but do not read it as the market rising.
weather.positioning: Read: Trend-following funds are neutral across the 18 markets they track, none is at an extreme and the size dial is 1.00, so they are not crowded and not a source of forced selling. Their lean is long the dollar (+0.45), energy (+0.15) and equities (+0.06), short ags (-0.14), metals (-0.28) and rates (-0.44). The nearest flips are estimates replicated from price: the Nasdaq-100 turns them buyers above 28,457.74 (0.15% away), the Russell 2000 above 2,832.86 (0.40%) and soybeans above 1,214.52 (0.08%), while they turn sellers on the S&P 500 below 7,455.07 (1.87% under 7,596.75) and the Dow below 51,049.51 (1.46%). A push through the Nasdaq and Russell levels adds a mechanical buyer; a 1.9% slide in the S&P adds a mechanical seller.
weather.volatility: Read: VIX is 20.83, higher than 82% of days in the past two years, so it is not quiet (calm means below the median); VIX/VIX3M is 0.98 and the curve is in contango. Single-stock volatility is 44.67, a gap of 23.52 points over the index, 0.1 points under the 23.62 level where the gap becomes a warning, and it is widening (+0.74 in 20 days), so a small further rise lights it. Implied correlation is 16.39, higher than 71% of its history, which means stocks are trading together more than usual and only direction pays. At VIX 25 protection is already expensive, 20% above today. Crown's volatility leg is dated 2 Nov.
weather.divergence: Read: One market-level warning is lit, momentum (RSI) not keeping up with price, out of the 8 checks, and 8 more show on individual markets. No single warning is a reason to sell; they matter when several agree with breadth, and breadth is broadening rather than rolling over, so this is a watch item, not a signal.
weather.call: Read: Crown's family is BROADENING_CARRY (own the average stock, collect premium against it) with a 1.00x multiplier on your own risk, shown as a data point and not a size. The fit is partial: broadening, a range that is not extreme, normal volatility gap and low trend-fund flip risk pass, but positive dealer gamma fails. The leading macro story is DOLLAR_SQUEEZE at 58% of its conditions, with GROWTH_SCARE within 12%, so it is contested and neither is a call. Next tests: ISM Services today 10:00 ET (23:00 SGT), jobless claims Thursday, payrolls and unemployment Friday 6 Nov, CPI Tuesday 10 Nov.
weather.cot: Read: Large speculators (CFTC data to 27 Oct, at least three days old, so it cannot time anything) are unusually long the Nasdaq, the Russell 2000, 5-year and 2-year Treasury notes and unusually short crude, natural gas and silver. For equities the crowded longs in the Nasdaq and small caps are the ones that matter: if the index keeps falling, that is the money that has to reverse. The crowded shorts in energy and silver mean bounces there would be squeezes rather than new trends.
weather.checklist: Read: The checklist is not read today. Every breadth row (today's green count, the 5-day count, monthly big risers, net highs against lows, stocks above their 20-, 50- and 200-day averages, the 4% mover ratios) is marked STALE because the panel carries the 3 Nov bar on only 37% of tickers against 95% required. These are AQE-list numbers, not the whole market, and they are blank rather than neutral: unmeasured breadth is not calm breadth.
weather.turning: Read: Now against 5 days ago against a month ago: trend regime downtrend, chop, uptrend; VIX/VIX3M 0.98, 0.92, 0.85, drifting from calm toward the 1.00 stress mark; SPY against its 50-day -1.62, +0.30, +1.53 ATRs, so it crossed from above to below within a week. The stance and the breadth thermometer have no values to compare. To turn this back, SPY has to be above its 10- and 20-day averages with the 10 above the 20, plus a weekly buy signal and a rising 5-day; the file prints no 'what would change it' list while the stance is withheld.
weather.themes: Read: True leaders, strong on the week and the month and near highs: Biotech (+5.54% week, +15.37% month, at its high), Insurance (+1.69%, +6.16%, 0.6% off), E-commerce (+2.2%, +5.71%, 4.1% off) and REITs (+1.15%, +5.82%, 4.5% off). Bounces off the floor, still 15% to 22% under their highs: Payments (+10.02%, +14.25%), Travel and Leisure (+3.9%, +2.72%), Infra Power, Infra Construction, Agri Commodities and Cloud Computing. Violent turns in broken groups: Solar Renewables (+4.26% week, -14.01% month, 51.4% under its high) and Crypto (+9.94% since the open inside a -28.01% month). Valen's own headline lists Solar Renewables as leadership but its table does not bear that out, so I read it as a turn, not leadership; Mag7 is down 6.83% on the month and Semiconductors 17.59%.
weather.groups: Read: This file carries no strongest-names list for the turning groups, so block 8 is a declared gap, not a list. What the sector table does show: Technology and Communication Services are graded TURNING (20-day -12.62% and -9.14%) but are still BLOCKED at the entry gate, while the leading themes (Biotech, Insurance, E-commerce, REITs) are already further along, not turning. Two of the six advances, ROKU and DIS, sit in the blocked Communication Services group, and the three Healthcare advances (EW, TMO, HNGE) sit in the one sector with a clean PASS gate; this is a place to look, not a list to buy.

ROKU.case: Unanimous: a fresh break to a new 52-week high at the pivot on 1.61x volume, advanced for the third time.
ROKU.why: It closed at 160.36 on its 52-week high, 0.09% from the pivot, with the 50-, 100- and 200-day averages stacked in order (155.15, 150.01, 128.26), relative-strength rank 84.01 and force building after a run of red bars (Elder impulse 8). Nobody argued against the name; the open risk is the group, because ROKU breaks out as one of two names in a blocked Communication Services group and the case dies if it breaks out alone while the group turns down. Buy only on a completed hourly close above 161.26 on 1.4x normal volume; the case is wrong on a daily close under 158.99.
ROKU.sector_note: Communication Services: graded TURNING, 20-day -9.14%, macro headwind, entry gate BLOCKED. No earnings date served.

plan: Before 22:30 SGT: ISM Services prints at 23:00 SGT (10:00 ET), so expect the first real move to come off that print rather than the open. Nothing is staged and nothing is armed.

At the open (22:30 SGT): do nothing on the six advances until a full hourly candle completes; closest to their buy prices are DIS (0.25% under 114.46), TMO (0.27% under 700.20), BRK-B (0.45% under 559.58), ROKU (0.56% under 161.26), EW (0.95% under 96.09) and HNGE (1.72% under 118.85).

First hour: judge the volume on the trigger bar as well as the price; the ROKU and DIS tickets ask for 1.4x normal volume, the other four carry no volume test and the objecting analysts asked for one. SPY holding 750.00 keeps the dealer cushion in place.
